content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To cope with type 2 diabetes, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Schedule a follow-up appointment with an endocrinologist (15 minutes)
Step 2. Review blood glucose logs to identify patterns (2 hours)
Step 3. Attend an initial diagnostic consultation (1 hour)
Step 4. Meet with a registered dietitian to create a meal plan (90 minutes)
Step 5. Purchase a kitchen scale for precise food portioning (30 minutes)
Step 6. Join a local diabetes support group (2 hours)
Step 7. Research low-glycemic index food alternatives (3 hours)
Step 8. Obtain a prescription for a continuous glucose monitor (10 minutes)
Step 9. Complete a comprehensive metabolic panel blood test (30 minutes)
Step 10. Adjust insulin dosage based on medical advice (5 minutes)
Step 11. Buy comfortable walking shoes for daily exercise (45 minutes)
Step 12. Learn how to properly use a lancet device (20 minutes)
Step 13. Create a weekly low-carb meal prep schedule (1 hour)
Step 14. Clear the pantry of processed sugary snacks (1 hour)
Step 15. Visit an ophthalmologist for a diabetic eye exam (1 hour)
Step 16. Establish a routine for morning blood sugar checks (10 minutes)
Step 17. Recognize persistent symptoms like fatigue or thirst (2 days)
Step 18. Discuss long-term health goals with a primary physician (45 minutes)
Step 19. Order a supply of glucose test strips (15 minutes)
Step 20. Log daily carbohydrate intake in a mobile app (15 minutes)
Step 21. Set a daily alarm for evening medication (5 minutes)
Step 22. Request a referral for diabetes education classes (10 minutes)
Step 23. Inform family members about emergency glucose needs (30 minutes)
Step 24. Perform a finger-stick test to calibrate equipment (5 minutes)
Step 25. Watch an instructional video on glucose monitoring (15 minutes)
Step 26. Shop for fresh vegetables and lean proteins (1 hour)
Step 27. Submit laboratory results to the insurance provider (20 minutes)
Step 28. Buy a specialized medical alert bracelet (10 minutes)
Step 29. Fast for twelve hours before the next clinic visit (12 hours)
Step 30. Search for reputable online diabetes resources (2 hours)
Step 31. Check if the local pharmacy stocks specific insulin brands (15 minutes)
Step 32. Feel motivated to improve personal health outcomes (3 days)
Step 33. Calibrate a digital weight scale (5 minutes)
Step 34. Practice self-administering a mock injection (30 minutes)
Step 35. Read a book on the science of insulin resistance (4 hours)
Step 36. Download a PDF of carbohydrate counting charts (10 minutes)
Step 37. Receive a formal diagnosis from a clinic (1 hour)
Step 38. Plan a menu for a family dinner that is diabetes-friendly (1 hour)
Step 39. Record a baseline A1C level in a health journal (5 minutes)
Step 40. Attend a workshop on reading nutrition labels (2 hours)
Step 41. Consult with a pharmacist regarding side effects (20 minutes)
Step 42. Subscribe to a diabetes-focused cooking magazine (10 minutes)
Step 43. Purchase a sharps container for needle disposal (15 minutes)
Step 44. Pick up a new prescription from the pharmacy (20 minutes)
Step 45. Weigh yourself to establish a starting point (2 minutes)
Step 46. Set up a recurring grocery delivery for healthy foods (20 minutes)
Step 47. Learn the symptoms of hypoglycemia (1 hour)
Step 48. Tell your employer about necessary medical accommodations (30 minutes)
Step 49. Undergo a professional foot examination (30 minutes)
Step 50. Ask for a copy of recent medical records (10 minutes)
